title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-05
content:
Daily scratchpad - GPU ops / infra personal notes
Date: 2026-03-04 (last updated)
Owner: Jordan Lee
Context: quick running notes for today and near-term follow-ups. Mostly todo list and short commands/logs.

---
Top priorities (today)
1) Check Dedicated pool capacity for eu-west-1 (Q1 reserved nodes) - urgent
   - Goal: ensure no capacity regressions for customer X during canary at 14:00 UTC
   - Quick checks: autoscale events, queue length, node utilization
   - Commands:
     - k8s: kubectl -n dedicated get hpa,pods -l pool=eu-west-1-dedicated
     - metrics: grafana -> infra/gpu-pools -> time range last 24h
   - Follow-ups: open/verify INFRA-2387 (scaling flapping)

2) Investigate intermittent pod OOMs on batcher-service (gpu-batcher-2)
   - Symptoms: OOM logs around 02:30 - suspected spike in batch size (client retry storm)
   - Quick repro steps: replay traffic from saved request set (s3://replay/batcher/2026-03-03)
   - Temporary mitigation: lower max_batch_size from 128 -> 64 on batcher config (canary on one node)
   - Note: watch latency increase on small requests after lowering.

3) Network checklist before kernel upgrade on gpu-nodes (03/06 maintenance window)
   - Confirm firmware versions for mellanox cards on all gpu nodes (target <= 5.8)
   - Reserve maintenance window with SRE and notify customers (scheduled email template in Confluence)
   - Verify backup SSH access path and jumpbox is patched
   - Run 'ibstat' and 'ethtool -S' on sample nodes; capture outputs to /tmp/net-checks-$(date +%s).log

---
Notes / quick logs
- Observed increased KV-cache miss rate 2026-03-03 01:20 -> 03:00 UTC. Possibly due to model rollout (v1.9.2 -> v1.10) on hosted-api. Opened ticket to product (PRD-145) to correlate.
- GPU utilization summary (last 24h): median 64%, p95 92% on eu-west pool. Idle nodes: 2 (scheduled for decommission? need to confirm with capacity planning).
- MIG partitioning: still using 3g. Consider moving one legacy queue to 2g to fit extra instances for cheap batch jobs.

---
TODO (short)
- [ ] Reduce max_batch_size on gpu-batcher-2 and monitor (15m)
- [ ] Run capacity projection for next 30 days (include Dedicated commit expiries) (1-2h)
- [ ] Send maintenance notice for kernel/firmware upgrade (use template) (5m)
- [ ] Validate NIC firmware on sample nodes: node-gpu-21, node-gpu-34 (30m)
- [ ] Add alert for KV-cache miss rate > 20% for 10m (create alert rule in Grafana/Prometheus) (20m)
- [ ] Patch jumpbox and rotate admin keys (coordinate with security) (30m)

---
Open questions / TODOs to discuss in sync with SRE (tomorrow)
- Should we increase reserved capacity for peak hours (12:00-16:00 UTC) for eu-west-1? Cost tradeoffs vs. customer impact.
- Rollout strategy for model v1.10 that caused cache miss spike: canary traffic to older runtime? fallback to v1.9.2?

---
Commands & snippets I used today
- kubectl -n dedicated get pods -l pool=eu-west-1-dedicated -o wide
- prometheus query: rate(gpu_memory_used_bytes[5m]) / machine_gpu_memory_total_bytes
- ssh core@node-gpu-21 'sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv'
- aws s3 cp s3://replay/batcher/2026-03-03/sample-requests.json ./ && python replay_bench.py --file sample-requests.json --target http://batcher-service.svc.cluster.local

---
Quick notes for handoff (if I get paged)
- If an OOM page comes in: check batcher-service logs, reduce max_batch_size, scale up batcher pool if needed.
- If network packet loss: check mellanox counters, reboot NIC after draining node if counters stuck.
- If autoscaler flaps: check HPA metrics and check for runaway heap growth in router service.

---
Reference links
- INFRA-2387 (autoscale flapping)
- PR #452 runtime: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/452
- Confluence: Maintenance procedures: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFRA/pages/987654321/

---
End of scratchpad. Will update after the 14:00 canary and during post-mortem if needed.
